subject: US-only processing, HIPAA enclave & HSM attestation request
messages:
From: procurement@mountwesthealth.org
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: it-security@mountwesthealth.org
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 13:22:00 -0500
Subject: US-only processing & HIPAA enclave requirements

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week. Mount West is evaluating Redwood for a production pilot that will process PHI from our ambulatory EHR and claims feeds. Before we proceed we'd like to confirm several procurement and security constraints so we can move to contracting. Key asks: 

- US-only processing: all processing and backups must remain inside the United States (no replication or fallback to EU/APAC).
- Dedicated VPC or single-tenant enclave accessible over private connectivity; customer-managed control plane preferred.
- HSM-backed key management (FIPS 140-2/140-3 attestation preferred) and BYOK support.
- SOC 2 scope and evidence for controls around access, data deletion, and logging; SIG/CAIQ answers if available.
- A short attestation letter stating Redwood will not proactively transfer data outside the US for this account.

Can you confirm these are supported and share the minimal evidence bundle we can attach to our internal security review? We are working toward a targeted go-live of 2026-04-01. Timeline and any procurement constraints (minimum term, onboarding window) will affect our milestone calendar.

Thanks,
Alice Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Mount West Health
procurement@mountwesthealth.org

Attachment: MountWest_RFQ.pdf (contains high-level scope)

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and the RFQ. We can support a US-only production deployment with the controls you listed. High level next steps I propose: 

1) Security evidence bundle: SOC 2 scope memo, SOC 2 attest (or letter of intent if SOC 2 report is out-of-cycle), our completed SIG response and CAIQ snapshot, and an HSM attestation template.
2) Technical kickoff with our solutions engineer (Dev) to validate the VPC topology and bandwidth/throughput expectations.
3) Legal to propose a DPA addendum with a US-only processing clause and standard HIPAA BA terms.

Dev — can you weigh in on connectivity options (VPC peering vs private connect) and confirm support for FIPS/HSM + BYOK?
Neha — can you prepare the DPA clause and a short attestation template we can sign and return?

Ill assemble the initial evidence bundle today and send a collated packet with links and a proposed mutual action plan. If it helps, we can do an intro call with your security team tomorrow.

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, procurement@mountwesthealth.org
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: US-only processing & HIPAA enclave requirements — technical notes

Hi all,

High-level technical confirmation and items we need from Mount West: 

- Deployment modes: Redwood Private supports a customer-managed VPC with private control plane or a single-tenant Dedicated pool inside a customer VPC. Either approach can be constrained to US regions only.
- Connectivity: we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and direct connect-type arrangements depending on your cloud provider. Peering is typical for low-latency EHR connections.
- HSM: we integrate with KMS providers and can use a FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSM for key wrapping. BYOK is supported; we can provide an HSM attestation template and certificate chain info.
- Logging & audit: per-route token-level logs, immutable delivery to your SIEM over syslog/HTTPS is supported; retention and export SLA can be configured.
- Data flow constraint: to ensure US-only processing we recommend network egress rules + account-level region pinning and a contractual attestation.

Questions for Mount West: 
- Expected sustained tokens per second or concurrent inference connections? (this drives sizing for Dedicated capacity)
- Do you need inbound connectors to ingest HL7/FHIR feeds directly, or will you push data into an S3/Blob staging area?

Im attaching our VPC onboarding checklist to capture technical requirements and to speed the kick-off.

— Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: VPC_Onboarding_Technical_Checklist.pdf (attachment stub)

From: procurement@mountwesthealth.org

Subject: Re: US-only processing & HIPAA enclave requirements — clarifications

Vivek / Dev,

Thank you — that covers most of our questions. A couple clarifications: 

- We prefer single-tenant Dedicated pool inside our AWS account if possible (isolated tenancy) and we will need to retain exclusive control over customer keys.
- HSM attestation: can Redwood provide a signed attestation confirming FIPS-certified HSM usage, a certificate chain, and a statement that keys will not be exported outside the US?
- Contractually we need a DPA addendum that explicitly states processing will remain in the United States and that Redwood will notify us of any exceptions (we expect none). Please include typical BA (business associate) language.

Timeline: we are on an aggressive procurement path and require contract execution and onboarding by 2026-03-25 to hit our go-live target of 2026-04-01. Please advise if that is feasible.

Security contact: it-security@mountwesthealth.org

Regards,
Alice Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager
Mount West Health

If the timeline to sign by 2026-03-25 is firm, please return redlines to the DPA and a completed VPC checklist (Ive copied the technical checklist). Well also share a short mutual action plan link to track tasks.
